title: Taylor 22lb Ultra-Precise Digital Stainless Steel Household Kitchen Scale, One, Silver
description:
About this item
Quality and precision: Taylor has been making precision products for kitchen measurement for over 150 years, Using only the highest quality components for accurate weighing. Measure precisely with an expanded capacity in both standard and metric units up to 22 lb/10000 g in ultra-fine 0. 01 oz/0. 1 g increments.
Innovation: sometimes during weighing the display might be covered by a bowl or plate - this scale has a hold feature that will "lock" In the last displayed Weight so the product can be removed and the final Weight can be read.
Versatile design: this product includes touch control buttons that won't collect kitchen dust or food particles. The weighing surface is durable, tempered glass that is naturally stain and odor resistant
Simple & convenient: weighing foods and small items should be hassle free, so this scale has intuitive features like auto-off (to conserve battery life), Tare (Zero weights between additions) and even a low battery indicator as a reminder for replacement.
Easy to read: the 1. 1" Lcd readout is illuminated with a bright backlight for easier reading in low light spaces.
Note: Place the item on a solid surface for accurate reading

reviews_1s:
Let me count the ways this scale disappoints.

It has a dead zone from 0-20+g. That is, if one puts something or somethings in this weight range, it may or may not indicate.

That alone is enough to trash it as being useful

A useful and dependable scale with a 0.1g+/- reading should have a threshold of at least that range, viz., 0.1g. This scale doesn't come close and worse still it is inconsistent as to when it will begin to recognize that a weight has been added.

Worthless

The scale display will cut itself off at random times. It has no memory. Each weight is therefore transient and unique. If one leaves an object on the scale, it will arbitrarily shut itself off and rezero after an indeterminate time.

Worthless.

That being said, when I carefully calibrated the scale after allowing it to equilibrate to ambient after a day or so, it seemed to be reasonably accurate with my calibration weights. I was mildly surprised.

That is about the only good thing I can say about this cheap piece of junk, other than it is attractive to look at, has a bright screen, comes on quickly, and has a large weigh table.

It is not dependable, doesn't have a pull out scale to read the weight of heavy, large objects, and the scale top is not readily removable for cleaning.

I bought this to replace my well-used. large capacity workhorse OXO 22lb scale, whose zero button has about been worn out as I can no longer find the OXO scale.

So reluctantly, I purchased this scale, though I have a decidedly low opinion of Taylor products in general from years of experience with their crappy thermometers and thermocouples. (I have a long and frustrating history with Taylor including their customer indifference/no service on personal contact.)

I should have known better.

Shame on me.

If one is buying a scale in the first place, it seems that one is interested in accurate (true) weight values and reproducible weights of the same object (precision). This scale is neither accurate nor precise, and it therefore doesn't meet even the most basic requirements of a scale. Why would anyone who goes to the trouble of weighing something want randomly inaccurate, and non-reproducible values?

If you are one, who needs a scale for both accuracy and precision (they aren't the same thing; look it up), then look elsewhere. DO NOT BUY TAYLOR JUNK, and DO NOT BUY THIS SCALE.Click to play video

I bake using metric measurements. I bought this Taylor scale in October to use at my son's house, but it has not worked properly since day one. The on/off button often fails to function, and I frequently have to press it multiple times to turn the scale on or off. Additionally, when selecting the tare button, it often turns the scale off instead.

I own a My Weigh KD scale, which is a brand preferred by serious home bakers. I've been using the KD scale for six years without any issues. Before that, I had an OXO scale that remained fully functional after many years of use, so when I purchased the KD, I gave the OXO to my sister. The only scale I found to be completely unreliable is the Taylor brand.Terrible scale. Thought would be more accurate since it reads a tenth of a gram but it doesn’t pick up the weight of anything unless it’s 4 grams or more. Wish I could returnThis scale just fell apart, top part separating from the bottom. It’s plasticky and cheaply made, get something more durable.If I could give this less than one star, or even no stars, I would.

I bought this so it could be used for my work place, but it doesn't give an accurate reading at all. I would constantly reference another scale in order to get precise measurements. The difference between the two scales (this one and one already used at work) would range from .2 -.5 of an ounce, and there's been a few times where it's an entire 1 oz difference. I can't afford to have those kind of mistakes when measuring at work, so I haven't really been using this scale at all, I've been using the scale that's been at my work place for some time.

The weight tends to fluctuate no matter how many times I've attempted to measure the same exact items. When using the tare function, the number on that changes as well, it also doesn't stay consistent.

I wasn't expecting that the digital display would have a textured, frosted appearance at all. If that's an issue for you, then don't get this scale.Bought as a replacement for an older Taylor model which lasted for 4 years.
THIS MODEL HASN'T WORKED RELIABLY SINCE THE FIRST DAY I TURNED IT ON. The tare function (which is mostly what I use the scale for) is very poor. The older model did tare perfectly. But with the new model, approximately half the time I weigh with tare (i.e. I place an empty container on the scale, turn the scale on, add an ingredient, expect to see the weight of the added ingredient), the scale remains at zero despite the ingredients that are now in the container.

As usual for inferior products, there is no customer service contact number.When I purchased my first digital scale years ago, I purchased a 500 gram weight so I could check it. I've owned a number of scales over the years, and they all read 500g (on their metric scale) and 17.65 (on their ounces scale). EXCEPT FOR THIS SO-CALLED "PRECISION" scale. It reads from 498 grams up to 501 grams. It's the most inaccurate scale I've ever owned.

It's also ridiculously large. Might make a good boat anchor. Maybe it should get two stars for being dual-purpose.I’m extremely disappointed with this food scale. After just two months of use, it has proven to be highly inaccurate and unreliable. The weight readings constantly fluctuate, sometimes swinging by as much as 50 grams, which makes it impossible to track food weights accurately. Even if you leave the scale alone, the weight keeps changing without touching it! Unfortunately, this scale has been a major letdown, and I would not recommend it to anyone who wants exact measurements.
